findings.title: Denial cache pins false denies and skips the DB re-query
findings.body: Check returns Allowed=false as soon as permDenialCache has an entry for (namespace, subject id, action, name, parent), before reading permissions or the folder tree. That entry is written for every DB deny and kept for shortCacheTTL (30s), and nothing deletes it when permissions are granted or the folder cache is refreshed. A check that races ahead of the creator ACL insert (or any deny followed by a grant, including a new wildcard/admin role) therefore stays denied for the full TTL even though the new re-query path would now allow it. The same stickiness freezes inheritance failures caused by a stale folder tree: once denied, later requests never rebuild the tree or reload scopes. A slow in-flight query that snapshotted pre-grant rows can also Set the denial after a concurrent request already observed the grant, so retries keep failing for 30s. This recreates the 'creator cannot open what they just created' failure on the retry that the PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type and collides on id 0
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey is built from checkReq.UserUID only, not the identity type or the canonical UID from GetUserIdentifiers. Anonymous checks use subject anonymous:0 and the renderer uses render:0 (both covered by tests), so both produce the same key for a given namespace, action, name, and folder. An anonymous deny of dashboards:read on a dashboard is then served to the renderer for 30s, and every anonymous retry refreshes that TTL, so image rendering/PDF of that dashboard can stay broken as long as anonymous checks keep missing. The reverse is also true for actions the renderer is denied. Numeric subjects (user:123) are likewise keyed separately from the resolved UID, so the same person does not share denial entries across id and uid forms, and a numeric id can collide with another identity whose id string matches.

findings.title: Denial cache key joins name and folder with an underscore
findings.body: userPermDenialCacheKey concatenates action, name, and parent with '_' and no escaping. Dashboard and folder UIDs may contain underscores, and parent is often empty, so distinct resources share one key. For example name=foo, parent=bar and name=foo_bar, parent="" both become ..._foo_bar_, and name=abc, parent=de_f matches name=abc_de, parent=f. A deny for one resource then returns Allowed=false for the other for 30s with no permission or folder check.

findings.title: Every newly denied resource reloads the full permission set
findings.body: If the permission cache hits but checkPermission is false, Check always calls getIdentityPermissions, which ignores the cache and loads every scope for that user and action from the DB, then writes the cache back. Absence in a just-refreshed complete set is treated the same as a stale cache. Denial entries only dedupe the exact same name and folder, so a sequential sweep of unauthorized resources (list filtering, many GETs) issues one full permission query per resource per 30s instead of the previous single query per user+action. Concurrent checks share one singleflight, but sequential checks do not.

findings.title: Denial-cache test still denies if the cache is ignored
findings.body: TestService_CacheCheck's explicit-deny case comments that the permission cache allows dash1 so a denial hit is the only way to deny, but it stores map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}. checkPermission treats a false value as no grant, and the fake permission store is empty, so a fall-through to the DB also returns Allowed=false. The test passes even if the denial-cache short-circuit is removed and does not cover deny-then-grant, renderer/anonymous key collision, or UID delimiter collisions.
